item.title: Thirteenth AVS payment, for some it will be lower
item.description: The 13th AVS payment will be paid for the first time in December, but it will not have the same value for all beneficiaries.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - First 13th AVS pension payment in December - Pension from 1 July: half the pension - Almost 2,7 million beneficiaries at the end of 2026 - 830'000 beneficiaries reside abroad
## Key facts | Term | Value | |---|---| | First payment | December | | Retirement | from July 1: half of a monthly pension | | Beneficiaries at the end of 2026 | almost 2,7 million | | Residents abroad | 830'000 | | Estimated average pension | 1'580 francs | | Married couples | maximum cap when the second spouse retires |
### Who can receive a lower amount
The 13th AVS payment will be paid for the first time in December, but it will not have the same value for all beneficiaries. The Federal Social Insurance Office (FSIO) has provided details on the first payments and indicated the situations in which the amount may be lower than a normal monthly payment.
For those who retired from July 1 onward, the 13th payment will be equal to half of a monthly pension. There will therefore not be the same amount for everyone: the sum will depend on the monthly pension, whose average amount is estimated at 1'580 francs.
In the case of married couples, the amount could be lower when the second spouse also retires, since the maximum limit applicable to married people then applies. The source specifies neither the amount of the cap nor that of the reduction.
For cross-border commuters, the cross-border figure is the one concerning beneficiaries residing abroad. The text indicates 830'000 people out of almost 2,7 million beneficiaries at the end of 2026, without distinguishing between countries or categories. It therefore provides an international figure, but no specific detail for Italy or Canton Ticino. ## The comparison between the average pension and the 13th pension payment
The source does not present a uniform amount for all beneficiaries. The most concrete comparison concerns the ratio between the monthly pension and the additional payment: for those who retired from 1 July onward, the 13th payment is set at half the monthly pension. For married couples, however, the amount may be affected by the maximum cap when the second spouse retires.
Applying only this rule to the estimated average amount of 1'580 francs, the calculation is 1'580 divided by 2, that is, 790 francs. This is an indicative proportion, not the official figure for every beneficiary: the average figure describes all the pensions, and the source does not say that every pensioner receives 1'580 francs. The calculation also does not allow the effect of the maximum cap on married couples to be measured, because its value is not provided.
The size of the beneficiary pool must also be considered without conflating different categories. The 830'000 residents abroad form part of the almost 2,7 million beneficiaries at the end of 2026, but the source does not distinguish cross-border workers from other residents outside Switzerland and does not assign a specific share to Italy. For cross-border workers, therefore, the relevant figure is an aggregate: it shows the presence of beneficiaries abroad, not the number of cross-border workers involved. ## The limits of the available data
The numbers provided by the FSIO describe the overall size of the measure, but leave some information open. The text indicates almost 2.7 million beneficiaries at the end of 2026 and an estimated average pension of 1,580 francs; it does not specify the distribution of the amounts, the number of beneficiaries per individual foreign country or the value of the cap applied to married people.
For the cross-border commuters' audience, the international figure should therefore be read as an aggregate: the source does not identify the professional category of beneficiaries residing abroad. The New Cross-Border Commuters' Agreement also remains outside the perimeter of the news.
The scope of the announcement remains that of the first AHV payments and the aggregated data reported by the FSIO. For the official pension framework, see [AHV 2026 overview table](https://www.ahv-iv.ch/p/2.01.i). For an indicative pension calculation, please refer to AVS pension calculator.
*Source: [rsi.ch](https://www.rsi.ch/s/4214055)*

item.title: Millions for Como: funds for cross-border workers have tripled
item.description: Over 9 million in the coffers of the Municipality of Como 6.492 cross-border workers residing as of December 31, 2024 7,81% of cross-border workers
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Over 9 million in the coffers of the Municipality of Como - 6.492 cross-border workers residing as of December 31, 2024 - Cross-border workers account for 7,81% of 83.135 inhabitants - 9.058.370,70 euro transferred through the Lombardy Region
## Key facts - Amount → 9.058.370,70 euros - Resident frontier workers → 6.492 as of December 31, 2024 - Share in Como → 7,81% - Prescribed threshold → 4% - National fund → 108 million euros
The Municipality of Como officially receives 9.058.370,70 euros through Regione Lombardia. The sum has been credited to the coffers of Palazzo Cernezzi; the increase in budgetary resources was formalized by a management decision of the Public Works Department. The transfer is the tangible effect of the new agreement on frontier workers cited by the source.
### The population requirement
The data used for the allocation are updated as of December 31, 2024. On that date, Como had 6.492 resident frontier workers. The total population indicated is 83.135 inhabitants, and the share of frontier workers in the city is 7,81%. The legislation provides for a minimum threshold of 4% for municipalities with more than 15.000 inhabitants. According to the source, exceeding this requirement allows Como to access regional funding channels directly.
The cited regulatory framework begins with the Agreement between Italy and Switzerland, ratified by Law 83 of June 13, 2023. The source also mentions the Decree of the Ministry of Economy and Finance of September 17, 2026, which followed the agreement, indicating that the fund thus reached a total allocation of 108 million euros nationwide.
While awaiting the final data, in the preceding months the authority had provisionally budgeted 3 million euros as a precaution, allocating them to the financing of construction projects and public works, including those subject to the non-extendable deadlines of the PNRR. Subsequently, the measure signed by the director of the Public Works Department, Luca Noseda, updated the budget with an increase of more than 6 million compared with the initial forecast.
The same decision established a dedicated revenue item called «Regional contribution for frontier-worker rebates». The final amount, already transferred through Regione Lombardia, thus replaces the precautionary provision in the accounting framework described by the source and increases the resources allocated to the planned investments. ## From the estimate to the recorded figure
### A comparison on two scales
The shift from the 3 million entered as a precautionary estimate to the 9.058.370,70 euro officially transferred is the central comparison in the matter. The first amount had been entered while the Municipality was awaiting the final data; the second is the figure incorporated into the budget through the Lombardy Region. The source quantifies the increase at over 6 million euros, and the headline summarizes the result by saying that the projected millions tripled.
| Item | Reported value | |---|---| | Conservative estimate | 3 million euros | | Official transfer | 9.058.370,70 euro | | Change from the estimate | over 6 million euros |
The comparison concerns an item in the municipal budget, linked to the budget chapter «Regional contribution from the cross-border workers’ rebate». The source does not report a breakdown of the sum among the 6.492 resident cross-border workers. The documented figure is therefore the transfer to the Municipality of Como, not a share allocated to each cross-border worker.
The percentage criterion also serves a specific purpose. 7,81% measures the share of cross-border workers in the total population of 83.135 inhabitants; 4% is the minimum threshold set for municipalities with more than 15.000 inhabitants. The arithmetic difference between the two values is 3,81 percentage points. This is a comparison of eligibility requirements for regional channels, not a rate applied to income or a paycheck.
The relationship between the figures and the budget clarifies why the amount had an immediate accounting effect. The initial estimate had been used to ensure funding for construction sites and public works, including those linked to the mandatory deadlines of the PNRR. After the final allocation, the increase expands the resources recorded in the accounts, while the source merely indicates planned investments and does not list individual projects or amounts for each construction site. ## The regulatory framework and the limits of the data
### National fund and local allocation
The transfer to Como must be viewed within a national framework, but the two amounts do not coincide. The source indicates 108 million euros as the fund’s total allocation at national level and 9.058.370,70 euros as the amount assigned to the Municipality through the Lombardy Region. The first figure describes the size of the fund; the second concerns the revenue recorded by Palazzo Cernezzi. The text does not show how the other funds are distributed among municipalities or regions, so the figure for Como cannot automatically be extended to other areas.
The new framework is traced back to the New Cross-Border Workers Agreement and, in the source, to the Agreement between Italy and Switzerland ratified by Law 83 of June 13, 2023. The official legal reference can be consulted in the text of the [Law 83/2023](https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:legge:2023-06-13;83). The next step identified by the source is the Decree of the Ministry of Economy and Finance of September 17, 2026, associated with the increase in the national allocation to 108 million euros.
The scope of the news item, however, remains that of the municipal budget and tax rebates. These are matters concerning the framework for cross-border workers, but the source does not use them to calculate the transfer to Como. For tax matters, the separate official reference is the [AFC information sheet](https://m4.ti.ch/fileadmin/DFE/DC/DOC-IF/nuovo_accordo/nuovo_accordo_foglio_informativo_FAQ.pdf); the municipal figure remains the one in the determination described in the source.
The source also does not indicate a list of works already completed, a spending timetable, or the share allocated to each project. It documents the accounting update, the planned funding for construction sites and public works, and the reference to the PNRR deadlines. For this reason, the documented effect is an increase in budgetary resources, not the final outcome of the investments. To follow the specific topic of Ticino-Italy tax rebates.
*Source: [comozero.it](https://comozero.it/attualita/dai-frontalieri-una-cascata-doro-per-il-comune-di-como-i-3-milioni-previsti-si-sono-triplicati/)*

item.title: Cross-border workers, proposed healthcare tax: 30-150 euros from 2027
item.description: The Meloni Government has passed a budget law that modifies the cost-sharing contribution paid by cross-border workers to the National Health Service
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The text provides for a fixed fee: 30-150 euro from 2027 - The amount will be decided each year by the region of residence - The old criterion ranged from 3% to 6% of the monthly salary - Failure to pay: administrative penalty of 100%
## Key facts - Effective date → from 2027 - Monthly amount → from 30 to 150 euros - Decision → region of residence, every year - Dependents → up to 50 additional euros - Penalty → 100% of the unpaid amount
The Meloni Government has passed a budget law that modifies the cost-sharing contribution paid by cross-border workers to the National Health Service, the health tax they are required to pay. The text is now set for parliamentary debate. The change concerns the payment intended to ensure greater funding for healthcare in border areas.
### The change in the budget text
Article 70 of the new Italian budget law provides, starting in 2027, for a switch to a fixed monthly amount between 30 and 150 euros. The amount will not be the same for everyone: the text indicates that the contribution will be determined each year by the region of residence. The source also refers to the individual regions concerned as the entities responsible for deciding the specific amount.
In the official paragraph concerning the salaries of former cross-border workers, prior to 17 July 2023, the effective date indicated is therefore 2027. For dependents, an additional maximum amount of 50 euros is provided. This concerns the new cost-sharing contribution to the SSN, not a payment described as a percentage of salary.
The proposal thus changes the criterion used to present the healthcare contribution for cross-border workers. The source does not indicate a single nationwide amount: it leaves the actual amount to the region of residence and sets only the minimum and maximum monthly limits. ## From proportional calculation to fixed fee
The comparison between the mechanism described so far and the one included in the budget text concerns both the calculation basis and the monthly cap. Before the change, the payment was linked to the monthly salary: the source indicates a percentage between 3% and 6%, with a minimum of 30 euro and a maximum of 200 euro for each month. The 3% and 6% are therefore the two endpoints of the specified percentage, while 30 and 200 euro are the monetary limits.
### The figures compared
| Item | Criterion indicated so far | New criterion provided for | |---|---|---| | Base | Monthly salary | Fixed sum | | Calculation | From 3% to 6% of the monthly salary | Not expressed as a percentage | | Minimum limit | 30 euro per month | 30 euro per month | | Maximum limit | 200 euro per month | 150 euro per month | | Determination | Proportional criterion | Region of residence, each year |
The comparison highlights a specific change: the new text does not tie the amount to a percentage of the salary, but establishes a monetary range. The minimum remains at 30 euro per month, while the stated maximum goes from 200 to 150 euro; the nominal difference between the two caps is 50 euro per month. However, this figure does not make it possible to determine how much each individual cross-border worker will pay, because the amount within the new range will have to be decided by the region.
The frequency is also still expressed in months: the previous criterion referred to an amount for each month and the new text indicates a monthly amount. The source does not provide individual salaries, regions with figures already approved, or simulations. Therefore, the comparison can describe the structure of the two systems, but cannot be turned into a personalized estimate. ## Effective date and penalties in the draft
The OCST, identified by the source as the most representative Swiss trade union, pointed out a positive element in the text: the provision would no longer be retroactive to 2024. According to this interpretation, collection of the contribution would begin in 2027, the same effective date reported in the paragraph on the fixed amount. The conditional verb reflects the status of the measure, which is still scheduled for parliamentary discussion.
In the event of non-payment, the draft provides for an administrative penalty equal to 100% of the unpaid contribution. The source does not indicate any other penalties, interest, calculation methods or recovery procedures; these elements cannot be inferred from the text provided.
The [AFC information sheet](https://m4.ti.ch/fileadmin/DFE/DC/DOC-IF/nuovo_accordo/nuovo_accordo_foglio_informativo_FAQ.pdf), listed among the official references for cross-border workers' taxation, concerns withholding tax on employment income, which is withheld in Switzerland. For new cross-border workers, Switzerland levies up to 80% and Italy taxes the income, with a tax credit to eliminate double taxation; former cross-border workers are taxed only in Switzerland. This tax information does not add any figures to the contribution to the SSN described by the source.
### What the text does not quantify
It does not address rebates or the New Cross-Border Workers Agreement either. For official documentation on the SSN contribution, the reference indicated is the [Ministry of Health Decree 11/14/2025](https://www.gazzettaufficiale.it/eli/gu/2025/12/18/293/sg/pdf). The scope of the report therefore remains that described by the source: monthly amount, regional decision, dependents, effective date and penalty. To compare the tax items on a payslip, tax calculator is available.

item.title: Health tax and rebates, working group soon
item.description: The working group will be convened shortly. The confirmation came during the meeting in the federal capital between a delegation of the Ticino
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Roundtable soon on the health tax and tax rebates - Bern, Rome, Ticino and Lombardy at the roundtable - Meeting in Bern with Guy Parmelin - Delegation comprising three representatives from Ticino
## Key facts - What → working group - Convening → shortly - Location → Bern - Participants → Bern, Rome, Ticino and Lombardy - Topics → health tax and precautionary suspension of withholding-tax rebates - Delegation → Marina Carobbio Guscetti, Christian Vitta and Piero Marchesi
### The outcome of the meeting The working group will be convened shortly. The confirmation came during the meeting in the federal capital between a delegation of the Ticino Executive and President of the Confederation Guy Parmelin. Representatives of Bern, Rome, the Canton of Ticino and Lombardy will take part.
The discussion concerns the so-called «health tax» and the precautionary suspension of rebates of withholding taxes paid by cross-border workers. These are the two elements listed among the main outcomes of the meeting. The reference to the cross-border worker is therefore explicit: the source links the rebates to the withholding taxes of cross-border workers.
The cantonal delegation was composed of President Marina Carobbio Guscetti and State Councillors Christian Vitta and Piero Marchesi. The meeting had been requested by the Ticino Government, with the aim of explaining the particularities of the Canton and the challenges it must face, as well as explaining the reasons for its recent positions on sensitive dossiers.
In the section devoted to relations with Italy, the Council of State set out its requests concerning the correct application of the new Agreement on the taxation of cross-border workers, referred to as the New Agreement on Cross-Border Workers. The source emphasizes the significant financial repercussions for the Canton, but does not indicate any amounts. The announced working group is the discussion that will be convened shortly; the report does not mention a final decision on the two dossiers. ## The tax scope of the roundtable
### Two related issues The text does not treat the health tax and tax rebates as two identical measures. The former is presented as an issue in relations with Italy. The latter are identified as the remittance of withholding taxes paid by cross-border commuters, with a suspension described as precautionary. The common point is the political forum identified for addressing them: a roundtable with representatives of the national governments, Ticino and Lombardy.
| Dossier | What the source reports | Venue or development | |---|---|---| | Health tax | Issue in relations with Italy | Working group to be convened shortly | | Tax rebates | Withholding taxes paid by cross-border commuters; precautionary suspension | Same roundtable | | New Cross-Border Commuter Agreement | Correct application of the agreement on the taxation of cross-border commuters | State Council demands |
The connection with withholding tax is relevant because the source does not speak generically of cross-border relations: it specifically refers to the withholding taxes paid by cross-border commuters and the financial repercussions for the canton. The New Cross-Border Commuter Agreement is mentioned in connection with its correct application, not as a new decision announced during the meeting in Bern.
From a tax perspective, the [FTA information sheet](https://m4.ti.ch/fileadmin/DFE/DC/DOC-IF/nuovo_accordo/nuovo_accordo_foglio_informativo_FAQ.pdf) distinguishes between new and existing cross-border commuters. For new cross-border commuters, Switzerland withholds up to 80% and Italy taxes the income; the tax credit eliminates double taxation. For existing cross-border commuters, taxation takes place in Switzerland (for new cross-border workers also in Italy, with a tax credit). These elements are part of the official tax reference and are not presented by the source as outcomes of the meeting in Bern.
The report does not attribute a percentage for the tax rebates to the roundtable, nor does it indicate a new method for calculating the health tax. The documented fact is the opening of a joint forum for discussion of the two issues and the reference to the financial consequences for Ticino. ## Financial equalization remains a separate dossier
The second major dossier discussed in Bern concerns financial equalization. In view of the entry into force of the revision of the ordinance governing the weighting of cross-border workers' incomes in calculating resource potential, the Ticino government reiterated its expectations.
The source describes this step as particularly important for Ticino. The request is for the canton’s specific characteristics to be given greater consideration in the system for distributing financial resources between the Confederation and the cantons. The reference to cross-border workers' incomes therefore concerns the calculation of resource potential and financial distribution between institutional levels; the article does not state that the change directly affects an individual worker’s payslip or withholding tax.
### The role of the technical groups The cantonal executive also emphasized the need to continue in-depth discussions within the specific technical working groups, so as to take greater account of Ticino’s particular characteristics. The source therefore cites two parallel developments: the discussions involving Bern, Rome, Ticino and Lombardy on the health tax and tax rebates, and the continuation of technical work on financial equalization.
For the SSN share, known as the health tax, the official reference provided is the [Ministry of Health Decree of 14 November 2025](https://www.gazzettaufficiale.it/eli/gu/2025/12/18/293/sg/pdf). The report does not summarize its amount, application date, affected population or calculation methods. Nor does it indicate the amount of the tax rebates, the duration of the precautionary suspension, the date on which the discussions were convened or the outcome of the negotiations.
Regarding financial equalization, the specific content of the amendment to the ordinance, the timetable for the technical groups or a final decision are not reported. What is documented is Ticino’s request that its specific characteristics be taken into greater account and the announcement of further discussions. To follow the specific dossier, consult the page on Ticino-Italy tax rebates.
*Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/ticino/politica/1960582/tassa-sulla-salute-e-ristorni-presto-un-tavolo-di-lavoro)*

item.title: Car veers off the road in Montano Lucino: driver injured
item.description: On Wednesday evening, at around 23:45, a car left the carriageway of via Roma in Montano Lucino.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Accident in Montano Lucino on Wednesday evening - Car off the road on Via Roma at 23:45 - Only one vehicle involved - Driver injured; 118 and the Fire Brigade responded
## Key facts - Where → via Roma, Montano Lucino - When → Wednesday evening, around 23:45 - What → overturned car, on its side in the middle of the road - Vehicles involved → one - Injured person → the driver - Emergency services → Fire Brigade and 118 medical personnel - Investigation → Carabinieri
### The documented sequence
On Wednesday evening, at around 23:45, a car left the carriageway of via Roma in Montano Lucino. The vehicle overturned and remained on its side in the middle of the road. Only one vehicle was involved in the accident, and the driver was injured.
The investigation to clarify the dynamics of the accident was carried out by the Carabinieri. The account thus establishes the essential facts: via Roma in Montano Lucino, around 23:45, one vehicle and the injured driver. No other personal or clinical details are reported.
The available time information remains approximate: the source refers to yesterday evening, Wednesday, and places the incident at around 23:45. For the location, both the municipality and the street are indicated, Montano Lucino and via Roma. The text does not add a calendar date.
As for the outcome of the intervention, the source stops at the initial treatment of the injured person and the investigation entrusted to the Carabinieri. It does not report any subsequent updates. ## Tasks indicated by the source
The most useful information for understanding the response is the distinction between the activities carried out after the alarm. The report does not present a single action: it assigns technical rescue to the Fire Brigade, initial treatment to 118 medical staff, and investigative findings to the Carabinieri to reconstruct the circumstances.
| Responders | Reported activity | |---|---| | Provincial Fire Brigade command on Via Valleggio | Technical rescue team | | 118 medical staff | Initial treatment for the injured person | | Carabinieri | Findings to reconstruct the circumstances |
Comparing these three tasks clarifies the scope of the report: the driver's injury is associated with the initial treatment, while the circumstances remain subject to the findings. The source does not say that the reconstruction has already been completed and does not assign a cause for the vehicle leaving the road.
The geography of the incident is also defined by two distinct references. The accident is located on Via Roma, in Montano Lucino; the provincial Fire Brigade command is listed on Via Valleggio. The time is approximately 23:45, and the accident involves a single vehicle. These are the specific details accompanying the information about the injured driver, with no subsequent outcome reported in the text. The text therefore indicates two distinct locations: Via Roma for the incident and Via Valleggio for the provincial command. ## What is not documented
The Carabinieri's findings are mentioned for a specific purpose: to reconstruct the circumstances of the accident. The text, however, does not report the result of this activity. The report therefore does not allow the cause of the car leaving the road to be identified, nor any other details of the sequence beyond those described: it was traveling along Via Roma, went off the road and overturned, coming to rest on its side in the middle of the road.
Information about the driver is also limited. The driver is the person identified as injured and, according to the source, received initial treatment from 118 medical staff. The name, age, severity of the injuries, any transport, or updates after the medical intervention are not reported.
The report also provides no details about any closures of Via Roma, traffic conditions, or other effects of the accident. It does not describe when the car was removed, nor does it indicate whether the stretch remained clear after the findings. These elements cannot be added to the account because they do not appear in the source.
The approximate time, the vehicle involved, the injury, and the three interventions remain documented: the Fire Brigade with technical rescue, 118 for initial treatment, and the Carabinieri for the findings. On this basis, the article reports the accident and the immediate operations without turning the findings into a cause or an already established responsibility.

item.title: Castel San Pietro: 2027 estimate in the red
item.description: The 2027 Budget forecasts a deficit of nearly two million Spending increases by 7.49% compared with 2026 PF at 75% and PG at 80%, both up by 5 points.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The 2027 Budget projects a deficit of almost two million - Expenditure increases by 7,49% compared with 2026 - PF at 75% and PG at 80%, both up by 5 points
## Key facts | Term | Value | |---|---| | Municipality | Castel San Pietro, in the Canton of Ticino | | Document | 2027 Budget | | Planned expenditure | 16'186’399 million francs; +7,49% compared with 2026 | | Estimated revenue | 13’408’950 million francs; +4,98% compared with 2026 | | Individual tax multiplier | 75%; increase of 5 points compared with 2026 | | Corporate tax multiplier | 80%; increase of 5 points compared with 2026 |
An operating deficit of just under two million francs is the central figure in Castel San Pietro’s 2027 Budget, in the Canton of Ticino. The Municipal Executive approved the message during last Monday’s meeting, forwarding it to the Municipal Council.
The budget provides for total expenditure of 16'186’399 million francs, an increase of 7,49% compared with the 2026 Budget. Revenue, including municipal tax revenue, is estimated at 13’408’950 million francs, an increase of 4,98% compared with 2026.
In the financial document, the Executive proposes separate tax multipliers for individuals and legal entities, with an increase of 5 percentage points compared with 2026: 75% for the former and 80% for the latter.
The Municipal Executive presents this choice as a way to partially offset the tax relief introduced at cantonal level. The two percentages are also described as being in line with the 2025-2028 financial plan, discussed during the ordinary meeting devoted to the 2025 Budget.
### Submission to the Municipal Council
In its general commentary, the Municipal Executive quantifies the negative result at 1’968’649 million francs and attributes it to the increase in operating expenses, while tax revenue and operating income grow modestly. The Executive presents the budget as being in line with its medium-term financial strategy, set out in the financial plan and policy guidelines, and indicates equity of more than 20 million francs.
The message thus brings together the expenditure forecast, the revenue estimate and the proposal concerning the multiplier in a single financial framework. The figures and percentages refer to the 2027 Budget and, for the comparisons indicated, to the 2026 Budget; the text attributes the proposal to the Municipal Executive and its transmission to the Municipal Council. The comparison between the figures is possible because the two changes have the same basis: the 2027 Budget is measured against the 2026 Budget. Expenditure increases by 7,49%, while revenue increases by 4,98%. The arithmetic difference between the two rates is 2,51 percentage points: the calculation results from 7,49 minus 4,98 and does not constitute a new percentage announced by the Municipality.
### Reading the data
| Item | 2027 value | Comparison | |---|---|---| | Total projected expenditure | 16'186’399 million francs | +7,49% compared with the 2026 Budget | | Estimated revenue | 13’408’950 million francs | +4,98% compared with the 2026 Budget | | Multiplier for PF | 75% | +5 points compared with 2026 | | Multiplier for PG | 80% | +5 points compared with 2026 |
The text does not provide the absolute amounts of expenditure and revenue in the 2026 Budget. Therefore, the comparison in francs between the two years cannot be derived from the data provided: it is documented only through the percentage changes.
The Municipality summarizes its explanation of the deficit as follows:
> «linked to the growth in operating expenses, while tax revenue and operating revenues show limited growth»
The wording therefore distinguishes three elements: operating expenses, tax revenue, and other operating revenues. However, the document does not provide a numerical breakdown of the negative result among these items, nor does it indicate how much each contributed to the deficit.
For those following the issue of cross-border work, the scope of the news remains that of municipal taxation in Castel San Pietro. The message refers to PF, PG, and municipal tax revenue, but does not quantify effects on employment income or withholding tax. It is therefore not possible to link the Budget data to a documented change in these areas. The framework described by the Municipal Executive also includes its own resources and the choices set out for the medium term. Equity is stated to exceed 20 million francs. Moreover, according to the Executive, the extraordinary surpluses recorded in 2018 and subsequent years made it possible to implement measures to redistribute these resources to individuals and legal entities in the short term.
The financial strategy referred to in the general commentary calls for containing expenditure under municipal responsibility and a significant reduction in the works plan, based on revised priorities. It also includes balancing the accounts of the drinking-water, waste and wastewater services, as well as an increase in tax revenue.
These points describe the direction indicated by the Executive, but the Budget text does not quantify the expected savings, list the works to be scaled back, or assign a specific amount to each service. The source does not even report the values of the multipliers applied in 2026: it only indicates the proposed increase of 5 points and the levels of 75% for individuals and 80% for legal entities.
### Scope of the news story
The document does not break down the deficit by expenditure chapter and does not specify what part of the increase in revenue derives from tax revenue or other operating revenue. It also contains no information on salaries, social contributions, transport or working conditions across the border.
Accordingly, no effects on commuting, permits or the tax rules applicable to work between Italy and Switzerland are documented. Based on the available information, the news story concerns the Municipality's financial situation and the proposal of its Municipal Executive for the 2027 Budget.

## TL;DR - On February 28, 2027, voters will vote on five issues - Nuclear power is the counterproposal to “Stop the blackout” - Foie gras and naturalization are covered by two initiatives - Collective labour agreements and cantonal minimum wages are among the items on the ballot
## Key facts - Date → 28 February 2027 - Issues → five - Nuclear energy → abolition of the ban on new nuclear power plants - Naturalization → after five years of legal residence - Trade agreement → EFTA and Malaysia - Palm oil → 12'500 tonnes - Labour → precedence of CLAs over cantonal minimum wages
### Five issues on the table The popular vote on 28 February 2027 will concern five issues. Among them is the abolition of the ban on building new nuclear power plants, a proposal that the Federal Council has designed as an indirect counter-proposal to the popular initiative «Stop the blackout».
The popular initiative on foie gras, which proposes banning its import, is also among the questions. The democracy initiative is also planned: it aims to standardize naturalization procedures and allow naturalization after five years of legal residence in Switzerland, regardless of the type of permit.
The agreement on free trade between EFTA (the European Free Trade Association) and Malaysia is also among the issues. The list is rounded off by the Federal Council's proposal to give precedence to collective labour agreements (CLAs) over cantonal minimum wages. ### A list with five different instruments The five issues are not presented in the same way. The source distinguishes popular initiatives, an indirect counterproposal, a free trade agreement and a Federal Council proposal. The comparison helps distinguish the items put to a vote without attributing content to them that the text does not indicate.
| Topic | Form indicated | Content described | |---|---|---| | Nuclear power plants | Indirect counterproposal | Abolition of the ban on new power plants | | Foie gras | Popular initiative | Import ban | | Democracy | Popular initiative | Uniform naturalization procedures | | EFTA and Malaysia | Free trade agreement | Reduction of duties on 12'500 tonnes of palm oil | | Collective labour agreements | Federal Council proposal | Precedence over cantonal minimum wages |
The two popular initiatives therefore have a directly stated objective: to ban the import of foie gras and standardize naturalization procedures. The counterproposal on nuclear power, however, is linked in the source to the “Stop the blackout” initiative.
For a cross-border worker interested in labour rules in Switzerland, the item on collective labour agreements is the only one in the news item that explicitly concerns wage regulation. The source does not, however, establish a concrete effect for a cross-border worker, nor does it indicate a new minimum wage, a sector or a specific canton. For naturalization as well, only the five-year period and independence from the type of permit are indicated. ### What the source establishes and does not establish The wording of the five points contains different qualifications, which should not be flattened. In the case of nuclear power, it refers to abolishing the ban on building new power plants and to the Federal Council's indirect counter-proposal to the popular initiative “Stop the blackout”. For the EFTA-Malaysia agreement, by contrast, the source uses the verb should: it indicates an expected reduction in customs duties on 12'500 tonnes of palm oil, not a result already presented as achieved.
The text presents both initiatives starting from their respective objectives: the one concerning foie gras seeks to ban imports, while the one concerning democracy seeks to standardize naturalization procedures and allow naturalization after five years of legal residence in Switzerland, without depending on the type of permit. The implementation arrangements, however, are not described.
For the cross-border worker who works in Ticino, the material therefore does not quantify any consequences for wages, procedures or other aspects of the employment relationship. Nor does it indicate results, committee positions, cantons involved or professional categories. The documented element remains the project concerning collective labour agreements and cantonal minimum wages; beyond this scope, the source does not allow any specific effects to be formulated.

item.title: Massagno proposes a tax multiplier of 77% for 2027
item.description: The Municipal Executive of Massagno proposes raising the tax multiplier from 70% to 77%.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Massagno proposes 77% for the 2027 budget - The projected deficit is 528'142 francs - Net investments amount to 7'732'000 francs - The municipal council will decide on 14 December
## Key facts - Previous multiplier → 70% - Proposed multiplier → 77% - Tax requirement → 25'314'750 francs - Arithmetic multiplier → 78,64% - Tax base: individuals → 95,65% - Tax base: legal entities → 4,35% - Operating deficit → 528'142 francs - Equity at the end of 2025 → approximately 10,9 million francs
The Municipal Executive of Massagno proposes raising the tax multiplier from 70% to 77%. The measure comes after two years of stability and, according to the proposal, is intended to address rising costs and financial uncertainties. The increase applies to both individuals and legal entities.
The 2027 Budget forecasts an operating deficit of 528'142 francs. At the same time, it provides for net investments of 7,7 million, specified in detail as 7'732'000 francs. The decision will be up to the Municipal Council at its meeting on December 14.
### Why the Municipal Executive is proposing the increase The Municipal Executive places the proposal in a context of growing pressure on the accounts. This includes the Canton’s financial difficulties, the increased burden on municipalities and the consequences of the votes on health-insurance funds. The text does not assign a separate share of the deficit to each of these factors; it presents them together as components of the financial framework.
The overall tax calculation represents a specific item: the source attributes it to the Canton’s charge for reimbursements intended for taxpayers subject to international double taxation. The estimate for 2027 is 2,3 million francs, compared with the 100'000 francs indicated for previous years. In the overall calculation, the arithmetic multiplier reaches 78,64%, while the Municipal Executive’s proposal remains set at 77%.
The proposal therefore concerns the tax requirement forecast for the municipality, amounting to 25'314'750 francs. In the Canton of Ticino, the case of Massagno brings the issue to the municipal level: the text relates costs, tax revenues and the ability to maintain services, leaving the final decision to the Municipal Council. ## Comparing the figures The change from 70% to 77% does not coincide with the 78,64% arithmetic multiplier. These are three related figures, but they are not interchangeable: 70% is the level that remained stable in the two previous years; 77% is the proposal for the 2027 budget; 78,64% is the result of the arithmetic calculation. The source indicates that the vote will concern the Municipal Executive's proposal, while the arithmetic value serves to describe the tax requirement resulting from the accounts.
| Metric | Reported figure | |---|---| | Multiplier after two years of stability | 70% | | Proposal for 2027 | 77% | | Arithmetic multiplier | 78,64% | | Projected tax requirement | 25'314'750 francs | | Tax base consisting of individuals | 95,65% | | Tax base consisting of legal entities | 4,35% |
The percentages for the tax base describe the composition indicated by the Municipal Executive: 95,65% individuals and 4,35% legal entities. In the available text, they do not represent either the number of taxpayers or the average amount paid by each category. Therefore, the figure makes it possible to understand the structure of the tax base, but not to reconstruct a single individual tax.
The tax requirement of 25'314'750 francs is also an overall figure linked to the new multiplier. The source does not break that figure down by taxpayer, income, or personal circumstances. The same applies to the overall tax calculation: the comparison between the 2,3 million projected for 2027 and 100'000 francs in previous years documents a budget item, not an amount assigned to each person concerned.
Another comparison concerns the periods. The deficit is projected for the 2027 financial year, while equity, amounting to approximately 10,9 million francs, is stated as of the end of 2025. The Municipal Executive presents it as a reserve to ensure continuity of services. The source does not specify that this reserve must fully finance the deficit or investments: rather, it records the presence of an asset base alongside the needs of the new budget. ## Investments and the scope of the decision The investment program amounts to a total of 7'732'000 net francs, an increase of approximately 1,24 million compared with the previous budget. The initiatives presented by the Municipal Council are divided between works already approved and projects still under consideration; interventions for which a financial allocation has already been indicated remain separate.
### Works already approved Among the approved works is the renovation of the Valgersa swimming pools, for which Massagno's share is 1,55 million francs. Work on the sewer system worth 1,5 million is also planned: once via Genzana is completed, the work will continue on via Madonna della Salute and via Morena.
The budget also allocates 350'000 francs to the PTL/PAL projects, 160'000 to video surveillance and 570'000 to the second phase of upgrading playgrounds and recreational areas. These amounts refer to specific items in the investment program, not to a general distribution of the deficit.
### Projects still under consideration The options examined include the construction of the Palco Urbano in the area of the former AEM warehouses, the reorganization of the Municipal building's spaces with the adoption of a new energy carrier and, for the recycling center on via Ciusarella, a temporary relocation pending the definitive arrangement. For these initiatives, the source describes the project direction without reporting, in the available text, a separate figure for each work.
The Executive wants to continue supporting associations and promoting environmental sustainability and innovation, also in collaboration with AEM SA and neighboring municipalities. On December 14, the Municipal Council will discuss both the 2027 Budget and the update of the 2027-2032 Financial Plan. The stated objective is to reconcile the investment program with balanced accounts while safeguarding the quality of services provided to the population.
For a cross-border worker, the only directly international reference contained in the text is the item relating to international double taxation. The source does not quantify any possible relationship between this estimate and a G permit, tax revenue sharing or withholding tax. There are therefore no elements to turn the municipal figure into an individual amount: the document describes Massagno's budget and the institutional decision, not a personal calculation.
*Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/ticino/economia/1960077/franchi-via-imposta-figurano-moltiplicatore)*

item.title: 62-year-old Neapolitan man arrested in Cassarate over financial flows
item.description: A 62-year-old Neapolitan man arrested in Cassarate on October 21 Approximately 50 million euros between July 2025 and March 2026 From Luxembourg
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - A 62-year-old Neapolitan man arrested in Cassarate on October 21 - Around 50 million euros between July 2025 and March 2026 - From Luxembourg, the funds were transferred to digital wallets - The 62-year-old man held a B permit in the Canton of St. Gallen
## Key facts - What → management of cryptocurrency flows, accounts and conversions - Where → Pero, Cassarate, Lugano and Luxembourg - Who → 62-year-old Neapolitan man and 51-year-old Calabrian man - Period → July 2025-March 2026 - Amount → approximately 50 million euros
On October 21, in Cassarate, a 62-year-old Neapolitan man was arrested who, in the documents of the Italian proceedings, is described as essential to the functioning of Pero’s “shadow bank,” dismantled in the Milan area. The reconstruction concerns a system in which, under the direction of ‘ndrangheta and camorra, funds from drug trafficking and tax evasion were allegedly laundered.
### The path of the money The path indicated in the documents is divided into several stages, but three steps are explicitly set out. First came the laundering through the issuing of false invoices. Then the sums were deposited into foreign accounts in Luxembourg. Finally, from those accounts, the money was diverted to digital wallets. The sequence distinguishes the financial starting point, the banking transfer and the digital destination.
According to investigators, the 62-year-old was involved in the operational part of the circuit. He handled the management of financial flows, opened the accounts and subsequently converted the money into cryptocurrencies. During the period from July 2025 to March 2026, approximately 50 million euros allegedly passed through his management. The account also links these movements to companies attributable to him: one based in Lugano, in the Canton of Ticino, and another active north of the Gotthard in the virtual currencies sector.
In the case, Cassarate and Lugano have different but both documented functions: the former is the place of the arrest; the latter is the headquarters of one of the companies mentioned. Luxembourg appears in relation to the foreign accounts from which, according to the reconstruction, the sums were allegedly diverted to digital wallets. The role described for the 62-year-old is limited to managing the flows, opening the accounts and converting the money into cryptocurrencies. The figure of approximately 50 million remains associated with the period from July 2025 to March 2026, again according to investigators. ## The profile between residence and prior convictions
From his period of residence in the Canton of St. Gallen to his prior conviction in Naples, the source reconstructs the 62-year-old man's profile based on distinct dates and locations. As RSI reported last week, he had lived in the Canton of St. Gallen from late 2022 to mid-2024, with a B permit. On Friday, it emerged that his criminal record included a conviction for fraudulent bankruptcy, handed down in 2004 by the Naples Court of Appeal, with a sentence of two and a half years in prison.
The information about his residence and that about the conviction concern different aspects of the account. The former indicates where he had lived and what residence permit he held during the period in question; the latter concerns a decision by the Naples Court of Appeal dating back to 2004. His role in the clandestine bank, meanwhile, is presented through the investigators’ reconstruction and the handling of flows dated between July 2025 and March 2026. The wording also changes: the conviction is described as a prior criminal conviction, while the transfer of around 50 million euros is phrased conditionally.
| Element | Period and place | Reported information | |---|---|---| | Residence | late 2022-mid-2024, Canton of St. Gallen | B permit | | Prior conviction | 2004, Naples | two and a half years for fraudulent bankruptcy | | Financial flows | July 2025-March 2026 | around 50 million euros |
The chronological comparison lines up three distinct moments: the 2004 conviction, residence in the Canton of St. Gallen between late 2022 and mid-2024, and then the flows identified by investigators between July 2025 and March 2026. Residence, a criminal record, and the disputed financial activity are different pieces of information, with differing levels of qualification in the report.
The source adds that the 62-year-old man often came to the shores of Lake Ceresio, especially in recent times. The reference places Lugano in two parts of the reconstruction: as a place the man frequented and as the headquarters of a company linked to him. The two elements are reported separately, but they contribute to defining the city's presence in the case. ## Recurring elements across investigations
In Lugano, the past of another figure identified as central to the affair also emerges. He is a 51-year-old man of Calabrian origin, one of the three people at the head of the «shadow bank». According to the report, he had already been involved in Operation «Aemilia», carried out more than ten years ago against the ’Ndrangheta in Emilia-Romagna and characterized by significant links to Ticino. Linked to the Crotone-based Arena clan, the man had facilitated the reinvestment of the clan’s illicit proceeds through a network of false invoices.
### The Arzo company The comparison with the Arzo case adds a second layer to the reconstruction. Last year, an Arzo company was among those under scrutiny in the «Mondi paralleli» investigation, concerning a tax fraud organized in the Brescia area by a mafia-style organization. The same company also appears in the records of the investigation into the Pero case. Together with other companies, it would have been used to carry out a fraudulent bankruptcy.
The concrete link between the various dossiers consists of recurring elements mentioned in the text: false invoices recur, as do the reference to Ticino and companies that have already appeared in other reconstructions. «Aemilia» is set in Emilia-Romagna and dates back more than a decade; «Mondi paralleli» concerns the Brescia area and dates back to last year; the Pero proceedings link the Arzo company to the records concerning the shadow bank. The report therefore presents different times, places and events, brought together through people and companies.
The verbs used also mark a distinction. The facilitation of the reinvestment of illicit proceeds is attributed to the 51-year-old’s past in Operation «Aemilia». For the Arzo company, by contrast, its use in the Pero case is expressed conditionally: together with others, it would have been used to carry out a fraudulent bankruptcy. According to the source, the picture therefore suggests that Ticino continues to offer organized crime a particularly favorable foothold.
*Source: [rsi.ch](https://www.rsi.ch/s/4206471)*

item.title: OSC nurses and unions call for salaries to be unfrozen
item.description: In the face of the block on the reclassification and yet another refusal, the unions and the Staff Committee invited Osc staff to Mendrisio, at 14.30
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Osc reclassification has been stalled for years - 2019: class 4→5 for nurses, 5→6 for specialties - Annual increases from 5'159 to 8'941 francs - Assembly on November 10 at 14.30 in Mendrisio
## Key facts - Organization → Cantonal Socio-Psychiatric Organization (Osc) - Adjustment → grade 4→5 for nurses; 5→6 with specialization - Annual increase → from 5'159 to 8'941 Swiss francs - Last formal request → January 2026 - Assembly → November 10, 14.30, Mendrisio
In 2019, the Joint Committee responsible formally established an adjustment for the nursing staff of the Cantonal Socio-Psychiatric Organization. According to the source, the planned change concerns moving from grade 4 to 5 for nurses and from grade 5 to 6 for nurses with specialization.
The reclassification would serve to recognize the training, skills and responsibilities required of those working in the delicate context of the Osc. The source also indicates a possible strengthening of the profession's appeal. Annual increases, depending on the role held, would range from 5'159 to 8'941 Swiss francs.
### A request still unresolved
However, the adjustment has remained frozen. Vpod and Ocst therefore continued their mobilization with the Staff Committee: after submitting a petition in June 2022, they publicly stated their position several times and sent the Council of State several formal requests, the last in January 2026.
After the latest meeting on the issue, the Government reiterated its refusal and, for financial reasons, denied recognition that the unions describe as already established by the social partners. In the face of the block on the reclassification and yet another refusal, the unions and the Staff Committee invited Osc staff to Mendrisio, at 14.30 on Tuesday, November 10, for an assembly.
The meeting will serve to take stock of the dispute and discuss actions in support of the claim. The source also notes that the meeting will address recovery of the cost of living for public, parapublic and social and healthcare staff, an issue connected to the petition and the union picket scheduled for November 24 at 18 in front of the Government Palace. Comparing the two classifications makes it possible to understand the pay demand without turning the stated amounts into an individual payslip. The source in fact provides the starting and ending classes, as well as an annual range, but does not assign each figure to a specific function.
### The class change and annual range
| Item | Reported data | |---|---| | Nurses | Passage from class 4 to 5 | | Nurses with a specialty | Passage from class 5 to 6 | | Annual increase | From 5'159 to 8'941 francs | | Difference between the extremes | 3'782 francs per year, calculated as 8'941 minus 5'159 |
Both described paths involve advancement by one class, but start at different levels. It is not documented, however, which function corresponds to the lower or upper end of the range. For this reason, the increase of 5'159 francs cannot automatically be attributed to nurses without a specialty and that of 8'941 to the other profiles.
The period is also defined: the text refers to annual increases. The source does not state a monthly figure, does not specify other components of compensation, and therefore does not make it possible to reconstruct individual net pay. The possible comparison remains between the reported annual endpoints, with a mathematical difference of 3'782 francs.
### Reclassification and cost of living
The demand for reclassification and cost-of-living compensation appear in the same mobilization, but the text presents them as two issues to discuss. The first issue concerns recognition of Osc salary classes; the second concerns public-sector, parapublic and social-healthcare staff and will also be linked to the demonstration on November 24.
The source reports that the Government justified the refusal on financial grounds and that the budget also blocks this salary adjustment. Neither the amount of the budget nor a specific figure for cost-of-living compensation is reported. The documented sequence runs from the decision of the Joint Commission in 2019 to the petition of June 2022, then to the formal request of January 2026 and the Government's latest negative response. The second event indicated in the source is the union rally on November 24 at 18 in front of the Government Palace. It is being organized by Ocst, Vpod and Sit. The rally concerns recovery of the cost-of-living adjustment for public, parapublic and social and healthcare personnel, while the November 10 meeting is convened for Osc staff and to discuss actions concerning reclassification.
### The scope of the available information
The verifiable connection with cross-border work is limited to the location and subject of the dispute: the news concerns the salaries and classification of nursing staff at an organization in Canton Ticino. However, the source does not say whether any cross-border commuters are among the employees concerned and does not provide data on their residence, the number of people affected or the composition of the staff.
Nor are the G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax rebates or withholding tax documented. Consequently, the text cannot be used to infer any specific effect on a cross-border commuter's social security, healthcare or tax situation. These elements remain outside the scope of the news, which focuses on internal reclassification and the initiatives announced by the unions.
The source specifies the venue and time of the meeting, Tuesday, November 10 at 14.30 in Mendrisio, but does not add the year. Nor does it document the outcome of the meeting, any decision on support actions or the result of the November 24 rally. Thus, the dates of the events and the unions' demands are available, but not any subsequent developments.
For a separate comparison on pay, consult payslip simulator.

item.title: Higher taxes in Bellinzona from 2028
item.description: The Bellinzona municipal government announced higher taxes from 2028, alongside the 2026 budget, which shows a deficit of 10,6 million.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Bellinzona: higher taxes from 2028 - 2026 Budget: deficit of 10,6 million - Tax multiplier at 93% only for next year
## Key facts - What → higher taxes from 2028 - Who → Bellinzona City Council - Document → 2026 Budget - Deficit → 10,6 million - Tax multiplier → 93% for next year
Bellinzona City Council announces higher taxes from 2028. The announcement accompanies the presentation of the 2026 Budget, which shows a deficit of 10,6 million. For next year, however, the tax multiplier is confirmed at 93%.
### The announcement and its dates
The news item published by the source distinguishes between two time frames. The first concerns the 2026 Budget, the document presented by the City Council together with the deficit figure. The second concerns taxation: the headline places the tax increase from 2028, while the text specifies that 93% applies only to next year.
The wording does not allow 93% to be interpreted as a figure already set for 2028. That number is associated with the confirmation for next year; the announced increase instead concerns a later point in time. The source does not report the new tax multiplier, quantify the difference from 93% or indicate an individual amount.
For cross-border employment, the usable information is therefore limited to Bellinzona, in the Canton of Ticino, and the timeline indicated in the announcement. The text does not specify whether or how the outlook concerns a cross-border worker, nor does it provide elements for turning the headline into a personal calculation. What remains documented is the location, the deficit in the 2026 Budget, the confirmation of 93% for next year and the 2028 horizon. ## The comparison between the three time references
The most precise relationship that emerges from the text is chronological. The 2026 Budget is the document through which the Municipal Council presents the situation with a deficit of 10,6 million. The confirmation of 93%, on the other hand, concerns only next year. The announcement of higher taxes is set for 2028. These are three references present in the same news item, but they do not represent the same information.
| Reference | Reported figure | |---|---| | 2026 Budget | deficit of 10,6 million | | Next year | multiplier confirmed at 93% | | From 2028 | taxes announced as higher |
The comparison avoids a reading error: the 10,6 million are not presented as the amount of the tax increase, and 93% is not indicated as the value valid from 2028. The source places the deficit alongside the 2026 Budget and the confirmation of the multiplier for next year, then points to a tax change from 2028. It does not, however, explain the relationship between these elements. Therefore, the deficit cannot be considered a cause of the increase, nor can the future level be inferred from 93%.
### What can be measured
The only direct numerical comparison is between the multiplier expressed as a percentage and the deficit expressed in millions: they are different units and refer to different dimensions. The former is a value indicated for next year; the latter accompanies the 2026 Budget. 2028, on the other hand, is an announced effective date with no associated percentage.
This distinction is also useful for a cross-border commuter. The news item makes it possible to identify the time horizon of the announcement in Bellinzona, but does not allow an effect on a payslip, withholding tax, or an individual situation to be calculated. The text lacks data on income, personal amounts, and how the measures are applied. The documented comparison therefore remains the one between the calendar, 93%, and the deficit, without turning it into a tax simulation. ## The scope of the available data
The source is unequivocal about the announcement, but does not elaborate on the information needed to determine what follows. The Municipality is identified as the entity announcing higher taxes from 2028, while the 2026 Budget is associated with a deficit of 10,6 million. The text also confirms the multiplier at 93% only for next year. Neither the expected figure for 2028 nor an amount referring to the higher tax is reported.
### The elements that do not appear
A reference to a cross-border worker therefore remains limited to the reading of the announcement in Canton Ticino. The source does not mention the G permit or tax rebates; it contains no data on AVS, LPP or LAMal. Brogeda and INPS do not appear, nor are withholding tax and double taxation addressed. These absences do not make it possible to establish a specific effect on the tax, social security, healthcare or commuting situation of someone who works in Ticino and lives across the border.
Nor is it specified whether the deficit in the 2026 Budget is presented as the reason for the tax announcement. The source places them in the same passage, but does not establish a causal relationship. For the same reason, it is not possible to infer from the 93% alone the amount of future taxation or to attribute to the headline a decision already detailed for each individual position.
The verifiable information therefore remains limited: Bellinzona announces higher taxes from 2028; the 2026 Budget shows a deficit of 10,6 million; the multiplier at 93% is confirmed only for next year. Everything concerning subsequent tax rates, individual amounts or connections with the taxation of cross-border workers is not specified in the source text.
*Source: [laregione.ch](https://www.laregione.ch/cantone/bellinzonese/1959787/a-bellinzona-imposte-piu-salate-dal-2028)*

item.title: Work on noise barriers on A8 and D08: guide to closures
item.description: The first week of November includes changes to nighttime traffic along the A8 Milan-Varese and the D08 Gallarate-Gattico Branch. Autostrade
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Nighttime closures on A8 and D08 from November 2 to 6 - First time slots: from 23:00 to 5:00 - Gallarate, Besnate and Busto Arsizio on the indicated routes - Second phase: from 21:00 on November 5 to 5:00 on November 6
## Key facts - Operator → Autostrade per l’Italia - Works → modernization and enhancement of noise barriers - A8 toward Milan → Gallarate-A36 Pedemontana Lombarda - D08 → Besnate-connection with the A8 - First window → nights of November 2–3 and 4–5, 23:00-5:00 - Second phase → November 5, 21:00-5:00 on the 6th
The first week of November includes changes to nighttime traffic along the A8 Milan-Varese and the D08 Gallarate-Gattico Branch. Autostrade per l’Italia has announced a plan of temporary closures to allow new modernization and enhancement works on the noise barriers.
The company has scheduled the work for the late evening and early morning hours. The stated reason is operational: nighttime work sites should allow the activities to be carried out safely, reducing the impact on daytime traffic.
### The first window: A8 and D08
The first set of restrictions is scheduled from 23:00 to 5:00 on the nights of November 2–3 and 4–5, respectively between Monday and Tuesday and between Wednesday and Thursday. On the A8, toward Milan, the section from Gallarate to the connection with the A36 Pedemontana Lombarda will be closed to traffic.
For those traveling toward Milan, the exit will be at Gallarate; from there, the detour will follow via Vittorio Veneto, via Sanzio, via Vespucci, via Lombardia, via Pier Capponi Mornera and via Buonarroti, then continue along State Road 33 del Sempione and State Road 336 della Malpensa, rejoining the A8 at the Busto Arsizio interchange.
During the same hours, traffic on the D08 will be interrupted between Besnate and the connection with the A8. Entry to the Besnate station will remain prohibited in all directions. The plan therefore affects two distinct connections: the A8 for those traveling toward Milan and the branch that leads from Besnate to the main motorway.
The measures extend beyond the Gallarate-Busto Arsizio section: the Solbiate Arno Albizzate access is in fact closed in both directions to allow maintenance of an overpass, as stated in the notice. ## Two windows, different routes
The plan clearly distinguishes the first nighttime window from the subsequent phase. Both the times and the section of the A8 affected by the closure change. The D08, however, remains closed from Besnate toward the interchange with the A8, with entry to the Besnate toll station blocked.
| Window | A8 | D08 | Directions | |---|---|---|---| | Nights of November 2–3 and 4–5, 23:00-5:00 | Gallarate-A36 Pedemontana toward Milan | Besnate-interchange with the A8 | Exit at Gallarate and re-enter at Busto Arsizio | | Night of November 5–6, 21:00-5:00 | Castronno-interchange with the Pedemontana toward Milan | Besnate-A8 toward Varese/Milan | Routes on state and provincial roads remain valid |
The times also allow for a direct comparison. The first time slot, from 23:00 to 5:00, covers six hours. The second, from 21:00 to 5:00, covers eight hours. The calculation derives exclusively from the time windows communicated by Autostrade per l’Italia and does not represent an estimate of travel times.
For travel toward Milan, the alternative route indicated for the D08 uses Provincial Road 26, State Road 33 and State Road 336, until re-entering at Busto Arsizio. For those traveling toward Varese, the suggested detour passes through the towns and leads to the Castronno entrance. Those heading instead to the A26 can use the Sesto Calende Vergiate entrance.
The second phase therefore involves a different exit point on the A8. Those heading to Milan must leave the motorway at Castronno and follow the signs for the ordinary road network until re-entering at Busto Arsizio. For entrances closed toward Milan, the instruction is to head toward Busto Arsizio; for the Varese direction, Castronno remains the reference toll station.
This difference makes the plan complex: in the first window, the main reference point for the exit is Gallarate, while in the second it is Castronno. The alternatives nevertheless remain anchored to the same local, provincial and state-road connections already indicated for the previous nights. ## The second phase and the locations that remain closed
The program will conclude with a phase scheduled from 21:00 on Thursday, November 5, to 5:00 on Friday, November 6. During those hours, traffic on the A8 will be interrupted between Castronno and the junction with the Pedemontana, toward Milan. The Solbiate Arno Albizzate and Cavaria interchanges will also be closed to entry.
### The continuing closure at Solbiate Arno Albizzate
The plan contains two provisions concerning Solbiate Arno Albizzate. Access remains prohibited in both directions due to maintenance work on an overpass. In the second phase, moreover, the interchange is listed among the entrances closed toward Milan. The text therefore links the continuing closure to maintenance of the overpass and places Solbiate among the locations to consider during the longest night as well.
On the D08, by contrast, the closure continues on the stretch between Besnate and the A8 toward Varese and Milan. In this phase too, access to the Besnate station will remain prohibited. For the D08, the alternative routes on the state and provincial road network already indicated for the previous nights remain confirmed.
The communication remains limited to road traffic. nor does it mention data on the Canton of Ticino, Brogeda, or INPS. These topics therefore cannot be linked to the plan on the basis of the source.
No traffic figures, delay estimates, average travel times, or extension of the works beyond the communicated time slots are provided. The available information concerns the closed stretches, the affected stations, the times, and alternative routes. The result is an operational guide to the overnight changes on the A8 and D08, with no additional information for assessing conditions other than those reported for the nights between November 2 and November 6.

item.title: SNL pension fund: SEV disputes interpretation of results
item.description: On October 30, 2026, from Lugano, the Transport Staff Union (SEV) challenged the interpretation given to the decision concerning the SNL Pension Fund.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - UBS will manage the assets of the SNL Pension Fund - ATIOZ imposed a new procedure after a conflict of interest - The funding ratio was 104,1% at the end of 2025 - SEV disputes SNL's results and communication
## Key facts - Location → Lugano - Asset management mandate → UBS, after Copernicus - Supervisory authority → ATIOZ - Union → SEV - Coverage ratio → 104,1% as of December 31, 2025
On October 30, 2026, from Lugano, the Transport Staff Union (SEV) challenged the interpretation given to the decision concerning the SNL Pension Fund. According to the note, the Pension Committee decided to entrust UBS with asset management, which until then had been managed by Copernicus.
According to the union, the decision would not attest to the navigation company's management success: rather, the procedure would have been imposed by the supervisory authority ATIOZ following a conflict-of-interest situation.
### The procedure imposed by the authority
SEV disputes the fact that, at the time, Agostino Ferrazzini simultaneously held the chairmanship of SNL and of the holding company at the head of Copernicus Wealth Management. The union considers the circumstance extremely serious and recalls that it had already reported it to the competent authority through a detailed formal complaint.
For SEV, precisely that overlap would have made a new procedure for awarding the mandate indispensable. According to the reconstruction in the note, the new procedure effectively excluded the possibility that asset management would remain with Copernicus.
UBS is therefore the manager designated for the Pension Fund's assets, while Copernicus remains the former manager mentioned in the matter. The objections, however, concern not only the transfer of the mandate.
SEV also maintains that Copernicus's management would have recorded performance markedly below average and management costs markedly above average. For the union, these results raise questions about the efficiency and appropriateness of asset management, while SNL's communication would have failed to address these critical issues. In the union's account, the issue therefore concerns both the origin of the new procedure and the assessment of the previous mandate. The comparison of funding ratios is the main numerical element of SEV's criticism. However, the figures do not all have the same date or the same basis: some concern the SNL Pension Fund, others Symova or the average of Swiss pension funds.
### The figures compared
| Reference | Funding ratio | Date or condition | |---|---:|---| | SNL Pension Fund | 104,1% | end of 2025 | | Symova Pension Fund | 111,97% | December 31, 2021, before the transition to Valitas | | Average of all Swiss pension funds | 117,1% | December 31, 2025 | | Estimate if remaining with Symova | around 120% | December 31, 2025, according to SEV | | Loss indicated by SEV | almost 8% | over four years |
The most direct comparison is between 104,1% and 117,1%: both refer to December 31, 2025, but the former is attributed to the SNL Pension Fund and the latter to the average of all Swiss pension funds. The arithmetic difference is 13 percentage points, obtained by subtracting 104,1 from 117,1. This is a calculation based on the reported figures, not a new percentage attributed to the management.
The 111,97% figure instead belongs to the former Symova Pension Fund and dates back to December 31, 2021, before the transition to Valitas. The SEV note describes a loss in the funding ratio of almost 8% over four years. If only the two figures 111,97% and 104,1% are compared, the difference is 7,87 percentage points: the numerical result is close to the wording used by the trade union, but it does not replace the period and context indicated in the source.
The 120% figure also requires caution. It is not the result actually recorded by the SNL Pension Fund: SEV presents it as an estimate of what would have happened if the employees had remained with Symova, with reference to December 31, 2025. The hypothetical condition is an integral part of the figure.
This makes it possible to distinguish three aspects: the figure recorded for SNL, the comparison with the Swiss average, and the alternative estimate put forward by the trade union. The source does not translate any of these indicators into an individual amount for employees, nor does it provide a personal figure for those who work across the border. SEV presents 104,1% as a figure that SNL's communication would have misleadingly emphasized. The criticism does not erase the number: it disputes the meaning attributed to that number in relation to the performance and costs challenged in connection with the previous manager.
### What is documented and what is not
The relevant passage of the statement is:
Calling the coverage ratio of 104,1% recorded at the end of 2025 positive does not remove the serious critical issues and does not redeem a management with disheartening results.
The content provided does not include the amounts of the management costs, Copernicus's performance percentages, or the method used to calculate the estimate of around 120%. It is therefore possible to report SEV's assessment and set out the comparisons indicated, but not to add a more detailed ranking or an independent verification of the results.
There is also no documented separate position from UBS, the ATIOZ supervisory authority, the Pension Commission or Agostino Ferrazzini on the merits of the criticisms. The text reports the trade union statement, the previous report to the competent authority and SNL's communication as described by SEV; it provides no other responses.
For a cross-border worker who was an employee of SNL, the relevant connection would be the pension fund and LPP aspect. The source, however, does not say whether there are cross-border workers among the employees, how many there are or what their pension status is. This caution prevents the matter from being turned into a general fact about cross-border employment.
No effects on taxation, health insurance, AVS pension provision or Italy-Switzerland relations linked to this specific decision are therefore documented.
The verifiable fact remains limited: SEV disputes the procedure, the previous mandate and the interpretation of the results of the SNL Pension Fund. To remain solely within the pension context, AVS/LPP and pension.
*Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/ticino/attualita/1960056/cassa-pensione-snl-il-sev-attacca-una-mistificazione-della-realta)*
